title: Hardship and Protective Holds — Updated Income Records for Long-Term Hold Status Reviews
content:
## Guidance

Under Hardship and Protective Holds, before each status review of a running Long-Term Hardship Hold, Ridgeline asks the consumer for updated household income records, because the review continues the hold only on income records that show the drop in household income still holds.

## When the request is made

The income records due date is fixed only after the hold's end date on record reaches past the status review the records are for.

Put the other way: as long as the hold's end date on record does not reach past the status review the records are for, no income records due date is fixed.

## What the request states

The request states the days allowed for the income records: the number of calendar days from the day of the request to the income records due date. The figure is a whole number of calendar days.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Hold concerned | A running Long-Term Hardship Hold |
| What is asked for | Updated household income records |
| Why | The status review continues the hold only on income records showing the drop in household income still holds |
| Timing | Before each status review; the due date is fixed only after the hold's end date on record reaches past the review the records are for |

## Tool card: `request_income_records_8e86e9ce`

**Capability.** Asks the consumer for updated household income records for an upcoming status review of a running hardship hold. One call records one documentation request for income records in the hold history, dated today, with a due date the given number of calendar days after today. The hold itself is not changed. On success the request and its due date appear in the hold history.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `request_income_records_8e86e9ce` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `hold_id` | The hold reference number of the running hold under review, read from the hardship hold lookup | Identifier |
| `due_in_days` | The number of calendar days from today to the due date of the income records (1 means tomorrow) | Whole integer of at least 1; no decimals, no empty value |

**Return.** A dictionary rendered as text with `request_ref` (the reference of the recorded request), `hold_id`, `document_type` (always `income_loss_evidence`), `due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `sent_on` (YYYY-MM-DD, today) and `status`, always `requested` when the request is recorded.

**Input and receipt (hypothetical).** Called on 20 June with `due_in_days` of 24, the request is recorded with a `due_date` of 14 July and a `sent_on` of 20 June.
